title: JANUS Tear Polynomial Quotient Conjecture — Adversarial Audit

naming_boundary.reason_for_C020: The earlier draft PR used C019, but canonical main already contains the connected-twin C019 cycle. This pre-admission audit is therefore advanced to C020.

source_bridge.computational_translation: A compact proof-learning invariant condensed from conflicts or residual states.
source_bridge.metaphor_boundary: Biological tear chemistry, emotion, salt conductivity, hardware P-N junctions and acoustic laughter are not evidence of a SAT speedup.

formal_candidate.input: CNF formula F and a residual or conflicting state alpha
formal_candidate.output: semantic tear payload tau plus a polynomially checkable derivation and, when SAT is preserved, a witness-recovery map
requirements: soundness: F entails tau or the attached certificate proves the claimed consequence
blocking: the conflicting state alpha violates tau
polynomial total payload plus derivation volume
polynomially many quotient states on every input
formal_candidate.conditional_consequence: If one deterministic algorithm satisfies every requirement on every CNF of encoded length L with polynomial total work, then SAT is in P and therefore P=NP.

two_sat_second_positive_family.tear: two implication paths x -> not x and not x -> x inside one strongly connected component

random_fuzz.comparison_oracle: exact brute force for at most eight variables

attack_results.reason: The canonical C019 SAT-neutral connector makes the primal graph connected. Both twins have total charge parity zero, so a single connected-component bit is (0) for both SAT and UNSAT.

The hidden Tseitin decomposition still gives SAT (0,0) and UNSAT (1,1), but the decomposition must be supplied as a certificate or discovered in polynomial total work under arbitrary neutral glue and representation changes.
The semantic parity payload contains two bits, while an independently checked derivation references a linear number of XOR equations or CNF clauses.

The current experiments decide structured families and prove local indistinguishability, but do not yet measure a residual-state merge count or a solver search-tree reduction against a controlled baseline.
No extractor is defined for arbitrary CNF, and exact residual canonicalization may hide SAT, formula equivalence, proof search or witness reconstruction.

positive: Tseitin parity is a valid family-specific semantic tear.
An odd Tseitin module has a polynomially checkable proof-bearing tear.
A SAT Tseitin member has a constructively recoverable witness.
2-SAT admits a different non-Tseitin SCC contradiction tear with polynomial extraction and verification.
negative: Primal connectedness alone destroys the naive component-parity extractor.
Two payload bits are not the full independently verifiable proof object.
The experiment has not demonstrated polynomially many residual quotient states for general SAT.

sharpened_missing_theorem.title: Universal Semantic Module Discovery and Quotient Theorem
sharpened_missing_theorem.statement: For every CNF F, a deterministic polynomial-time procedure discovers a polynomial-volume family of sound semantic modules and proof-bearing tears such that the induced residual-state quotient is satisfiability preserving, supports SAT witness recovery, and saturates to a polynomial UNSAT certificate when no witness exists.
sharpened_missing_theorem.anti_hidden_solver_clause: The module discovery, equivalence test, canonicalization, proof construction and witness-recovery annotations are all charged to the same polynomial total-work budget.

monsters_corporation_bridge.tear_channel: negative knowledge: a compact certificate that a family of worlds is impossible
monsters_corporation_bridge.laughter_channel_candidate: positive knowledge: a compact constructive witness and recovery map showing that at least one world is possible
monsters_corporation_bridge.collider_rule: A complete solver architecture must account for both impossibility condensation and constructive witness recovery; negative learning alone is insufficient for SAT completeness.

passed: exact C018/C019 Tseitin semantics through radius 8
polynomial verifier for generated odd-XOR module certificates
second positive family: 2-SAT SCC contradiction tear
open: positive compression result on a genuinely NP-complete non-XOR benchmark
measured solver-state merge counts and total-work comparison
universal polynomial bound on tear count and derivation volume

claim_boundary: C020 validates the Tear vocabulary on two polynomially structured families and rejects a naive extractor on connected C019 twins. It does not prove a universal tear basis, SAT in P, P=NP or any physical effect of biological tears.
